subject: science

concepts.title: Electric Current and Charge
concepts.definition: The flow rate of electric charges through a given cross-sectional area of a conductor over time.
concepts.key_idea: Electric current measures charge transfer per unit time in amperes.
question_patterns: find the electric current when charge ... flows in time ...
calculate the charge flowing through a circuit given current and time
how much electric charge flows when a current of ... drawn for ...
determine the time required for a charge of ... to flow with current ...
what is the current produced by a charge of ... flowing for ... seconds

solution_steps.explain: charge equals current multiplied by time duration in seconds

solution_steps.action: convert time to seconds if given in minutes
solution_steps.explain: when time is given in minutes, multiply by 60 to obtain seconds before computing charge

solution_steps.action: state the final charge with correct unit
solution_steps.explain: express the result in coulombs, since one ampere of current carries one coulomb of charge per second

concepts.title: Electric Potential Difference
concepts.definition: The work required to move a unit positive charge from one point to another in an electric circuit.
concepts.key_idea: Potential difference measures electrical work per unit charge in volts.
question_patterns: find the work done moving a charge across potential difference
calculate the potential difference given work done and charge
how much energy is transferred when charge ... moves through potential difference ...
determine the charge moved when work done is ... and potential difference is ...
what is the work done in transferring a charge of ...

solution_steps.explain: work done equals potential difference multiplied by electric charge
the work done in moving charge through a potential difference equals the electrical energy transferred, in joules

solution_steps.action: state the result with correct unit
solution_steps.explain: express work done or energy in joules, since one volt times one coulomb equals one joule

concepts.title: Circuit Symbols and Schematic Diagrams
concepts.definition: Standardized visual representations used to depict electrical elements and their interconnections in a circuit diagram.
concepts.key_idea: Schematic diagrams use standard symbols for cells, switches, meters, and resistors.
question_patterns: identify the circuit symbol for a resistor or variable resistance
draw the schematic symbol for a plug key or voltmeter
what does the symbol of a wire joint or crossing represent
verify the connection rule for ammeter and voltmeter in a circuit
justify why circuit symbols and schematic diagrams matters

solution_steps.explain: match the provided symbol to the corresponding standard electrical device
ammeters must be in series and voltmeters must be parallel across components

solution_steps.action: confirm the schematic follows standard conventions
solution_steps.explain: ensure wires are drawn as straight lines, junctions are marked with dots, and components use their correct standardized symbols for an unambiguous diagram.

concepts.title: Ohm's Law
concepts.definition: For a metallic conductor kept at one temperature, the current flowing through it grows in step with the voltage applied between its ends.
concepts.key_idea: Resistance is the ratio of potential difference to current for a conductor.
question_patterns: find the resistance of a resistor given potential difference and current
calculate the current through a conductor given voltage and resistance
how much current flows through a bulb of resistance ... connected to ...
determine the voltage across a resistor of ... carrying current ...
what is the potential difference needed to draw a current of ...

solution_steps.explain: divide potential difference by electrical resistance

solution_steps.action: calculate resistance if voltage and current are given
solution_steps.explain: rearrange Ohm's law so resistance equals voltage divided by current

solution_steps.action: state the result with correct unit
solution_steps.explain: express current in amperes and resistance in ohms, confirming the values satisfy Ohm's law V = I x R

concepts.title: Factors Affecting Resistance and Electrical Resistivity
concepts.definition: Resistance varies in direct proportion with conductor length and in inverse proportion with cross-sectional area, multiplied by material resistivity.
concepts.key_idea: Resistivity is an intrinsic material property measuring opposition to charge flow.
question_patterns: find the resistivity of a wire given length, diameter, and resistance
calculate the resistance of a wire of given length and area
how much does resistance change when wire length is doubled
determine the length of wire needed for a specified resistance
what is the new resistance when area of cross section changes

solution_steps.explain: cross-sectional area equals pi times diameter squared divided by 4
resistivity equals resistance multiplied by area divided by length

solution_steps.action: state the resistivity with correct unit
solution_steps.explain: express resistivity in ohm-meters, which is the intrinsic material property independent of wire dimensions

concepts.title: Resistors in Series
concepts.definition: When multiple resistors are joined end to end in a single line, the total resistance is the sum of individual resistances while current remains uniform.
concepts.key_idea: Series connection adds individual resistances and maintains equal current through all components.
question_patterns: find the equivalent resistance of resistors connected in series
calculate total current in a series circuit with battery voltage
how much voltage drops across individual resistors in series
determine total resistance for three series connected resistors
what is the total resistance when ... and ... are in series

solution_steps.explain: total series resistance equals sum of r1, r2, and r3
divide supply voltage by total series resistance

solution_steps.action: calculate voltage drop across each resistor
solution_steps.explain: in a series circuit the same current flows through all resistors, so each voltage drop equals current times that resistor's value

concepts.title: Resistors in Parallel
concepts.definition: When resistors are joined across common points, the inverse of total resistance equals the sum of inverses of individual resistances, and voltage across branches is identical.
concepts.key_idea: Parallel connection reduces total resistance and splits current among branches.
question_patterns: find the equivalent resistance of resistors in parallel
calculate branch currents for parallel connected resistors
how much is the total current in a parallel circuit
determine equivalent parallel resistance for given values
what is the total current drawn from source by parallel resistors

solution_steps.explain: sum reciprocals of individual resistances
take reciprocal of sum of inverses
divide source voltage by equivalent parallel resistance

concepts.title: Heating Effect of Electric Current and Joule's Law
concepts.definition: Electrical energy changed into thermal energy in a conductor varies in direct proportion with current squared, resistance, and time duration.
concepts.key_idea: Joule heating converts electrical energy to heat energy in resistive components.
question_patterns: find the heat produced in a resistor given current, resistance and time
calculate heat generated when charge moves across potential difference
how much heat is developed in ... seconds by a current of ...
determine potential difference across resistor given heat and time
what is the rate of heat generation in a heating element

solution_steps.explain: heat generated equals square of current times resistance times time

solution_steps.action: calculate heat from potential difference if needed
solution_steps.explain: using V = I x R, heat can also be expressed as voltage squared times time divided by resistance

solution_steps.action: state the heat energy with correct unit
solution_steps.explain: express the result in joules, confirming Joule's law that heat is proportional to current squared, resistance, and time

concepts.title: Electric Power
concepts.definition: The speed with which electric energy is consumed or changed into other forms of energy in an electric circuit.
concepts.key_idea: Electric power measures the rate of energy consumption in watts.
question_patterns: find the electric power of an appliance given voltage and current
calculate current drawn by a device of given power rating and voltage
how much power is consumed when voltage is ... and resistance is ...
determine resistance of a bulb from its rated power and voltage
what is the power rating of an electric device

solution_steps.explain: multiply potential difference by electric current

solution_steps.action: calculate power using resistance if needed
solution_steps.explain: using Ohm's law, power can also be computed as current squared times resistance or voltage squared divided by resistance

solution_steps.action: state the power with correct unit
solution_steps.explain: express power in watts, where one watt equals one joule per second, representing the rate of energy consumption

concepts.title: Commercial Unit of Electrical Energy and Electricity Bill Calculation
concepts.definition: Commercial electrical energy is calculated in kilowatt-hours (kWh) and multiplied by cost rate per unit to determine electricity expenses.
concepts.key_idea: Electrical energy consumption is billed in units of kilowatt-hours.
question_patterns: find the commercial electrical energy consumed in kWh
calculate the cost of operating an appliance for a given duration
how much does it cost to run a heater of power ... for ... hours
determine the total energy in kWh used by multiple appliances
what is the expense of electrical energy at rate per unit

solution_steps.explain: multiply power in watts by daily hours and number of days divided by 1000
multiply total energy in kWh by unit price rate

solution_steps.action: state the total energy and cost with correct units
solution_steps.explain: express energy in kilowatt-hours (units) and cost in rupees, confirming the commercial billing calculation

worked_examples.question_pattern: A current of {current} A is drawn by a filament of an electric bulb for {time_min} minutes. Find the amount of electric charge that flows through the circuit.

solution_template.explain: multiply minutes by 60 to obtain seconds
charge equals current multiplied by time in seconds

worked_examples.question_pattern: How much work is done in moving a charge of {charge} C across two points having a potential difference {potential_difference} V?

solution_template.explain: work done equals potential difference times charge

worked_examples.question_pattern: How much current will an electric bulb draw from a {voltage} V source, if the resistance of the bulb filament is {resistance} ohm?

solution_template.explain: current equals voltage divided by resistance

worked_examples.question_pattern: The potential difference between terminals of an electric heater is {voltage1} V when it draws a current of {current1} A. What current will the heater draw if potential difference is increased to {voltage2} V?

solution_template.explain: resistance equals initial voltage divided by initial current
new current equals new voltage divided by calculated resistance

worked_examples.question_pattern: Resistance of a metal wire of length {length} m is {resistance} ohm at 20°C. If the diameter of the wire is {diameter} m, what will be the resistivity of the metal?

solution_template.explain: area equals pi times diameter squared divided by 4
resistivity equals resistance times area divided by length

worked_examples.question_pattern: An electric lamp of resistance {r1} ohm and a conductor of {r2} ohm resistance are connected in series to a {voltage} V battery. Calculate total resistance and total current.

solution_template.explain: total resistance equals sum of r1 and r2
total current equals voltage divided by total series resistance

worked_examples.question_pattern: Resistors {r1} ohm, {r2} ohm and {r3} ohm are connected in parallel across a {voltage} V battery. Calculate individual branch currents and total resistance.

solution_template.explain: i1 equals voltage divided by r1
i2 equals voltage divided by r2
i3 equals voltage divided by r3
total current equals sum of i1, i2 and i3
total resistance equals voltage divided by total current

worked_examples.question_pattern: An electric iron consumes energy at a rate of {power_max} W at maximum heating from a {voltage} V supply. What are the current and resistance?

solution_template.explain: current equals power divided by voltage
resistance equals voltage divided by current

worked_examples.question_pattern: {heat} J of heat is produced each second in a {resistance} ohm resistance. Find the potential difference across the resistor.

solution_template.explain: current equals square root of heat divided by product of resistance and time
voltage equals current multiplied by resistance

worked_examples.question_pattern: An electric bulb is connected to a {voltage} V generator drawing {current} A current. What is the power of the bulb?

solution_template.explain: power equals voltage multiplied by current

worked_examples.question_pattern: An electric refrigerator rated {power_watts} W operates {hours} hour/day. What is the cost of energy to operate it for {days} days at Rs {rate_per_kwh} per kWh?

solution_template.explain: energy in kWh equals power in watts times daily hours times days divided by 1000
total cost equals energy in kWh times rate per kWh
